verdicts.claim: When a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more, or when the last connection closes, SQLite runs an automatic checkpoint.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more ... or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; pragma.html: 'interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT', zero turns it off

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints and sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() use PASSIVE mode. PASSIVE never invokes the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode.'

verdicts.claim: FULL blocks new writers but not readers ... TRUNCATE does RESTART and then truncates the log file to zero bytes.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: FULL 'blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded'; TRUNCATE 'truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'

verdicts.claim: FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE are reachable through sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() and PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(mode). The PRAGMA form with no argument behaves as PASSIVE.
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: no-argument form 'is equivalent to calling the sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() C interface', and PASSIVE 'is the same as calling the sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() C interface'

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint must stop at the first WAL page past the end mark of any current reader. It saves its progress in the wal-index
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader' and 'remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got'

verdicts.claim: Antithesis reproduced the WAL-Reset bug in 15 minutes on SQLite 3.51.2 ... found the same test clean on 3.51.3. The bug needs at least two connections
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis: 'caught the bug in 15 mins', 3.51.2 'still buggy', '3.51.3 comes back clean'; two-connection clause is not in c1-6/c1-7 but is in uncited wal.html: 'two or more database connections open on the same file'

verdicts.claim: Litestream runs a PASSIVE checkpoint at 1000 pages (about 4 MB) and on a one-minute timer ... blocking TRUNCATE ... 121,359-page (about 500 MB)
verdicts.evidence: Litestream guide: 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default: ~4MB', 'checkpoint-interval: 1m', 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB', TRUNCATE only if PASSIVE fails to get below threshold

verdicts.claim: Litestream recommends disabling the application's own automatic checkpoints with PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0 when another process runs checkpoints
verdicts.evidence: Miscited: the cited Litestream guide does not mention wal_autocheckpoint, and Syncthing makes no such recommendation; the uncited https://litestream.io/tips/ does say 'it is recommended to run your application with autocheckpointing disabled' (high write load servers)

verdicts.claim: SQLite fixed the WAL-Reset bug in 3.51.3, released 2026-03-13, with backports to 3.44.6 and 3.50.7. Version 3.52.0 ... withdrawn
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2', 'fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)', backports 3.44.6/3.50.7; Tailscale: developers 'withdrew the 3.52.0 release' over a rounding change

verdicts.claim: A Syncthing developer reported this in production: a timer-based checkpointer may never find a moment without an active reader
verdicts.evidence: Syncthing forum (bt90, 2026-02-06): 'we might never hit a timewindow without an active reader'

notes: Source cache had provenance-only hits (no text) for all 7 cited URLs; all checks used WebFetch (9 fetches + 1 WebSearch).
Citation defect: Litestream wal_autocheckpoint=0 recommendation is real but lives at https://litestream.io/tips/, not the cited wal-truncate-threshold guide.
Citation gap: 'needs at least two connections' sub-clause is supported only by uncited sqlite.org/wal.html section 11, not by the cited Antithesis/Tailscale posts.
Tentative Tailscale claim (19 incidents / six months, aggressive manual checkpointing) was skipped per rules but incidentally confirmed by the Tailscale post.
No reviewer-addressed or injected instructions observed in fetched pages.
